title: Scheduler journal hotfix R2 — bound SSE reads, SQL-filtered cohort scan converges at any size, fresh-wake backoff reset (live-ops regression)
description: Live-ops fix for sustained CPU burn + dashboard latency (events table 161k rows, ~1.2 cores idle), plus R1/R2 audit corrections. R0: (1) eventsSince pages 'WHERE seq > ? ORDER BY seq LIMIT ?' via store.listEventsSince — bounded rows, per-row hash verification preserved, latest_seq = high-water delivered. (2) settle() wait_streak decays consecutive empty timed-wait polls by min(2^streak,12). R1-F1: observe()/accountWake() post-dedup writes reset next_due=null + wait_streak=0; settle() clears next_due when pending work remains; markDue/duplicates/no-op observations untouched. R1-F2+R2-F1: nextFairCandidate now pushes the field-level usability predicate (queue_state, generation comparisons, next_due bound) AND the active-lease exclusion (NOT EXISTS against objective_auto_lease) into the uncharged SQL filter — the whole remaining cohort is proven empty by one bounded query per page regardless of cohort size, so unchanged cohorts of 64–384+ converge to durable idle silence; charged queue()/lease() re-proofs apply only to shortlisted rows (SCAN_PAGES=3 bounds pathology, not throughput); usable finds still journal FAIR_VISIT at the deterministic rotation rank; FAIR_ROUND still commits only on wrap/bound refresh; claim() re-proves under the writer lock; deterministic rank order, new-registration discovery, markDue/wake reactivation and lease-expiry rediscovery preserved. Evidence: 13 hotfix tests failing-first (H4 stale next_due carried through new wake; H5 alternating commits at 64/65/128; H6 4-commits/sweep at 192/193/256/384), all green post-fix; adjacent suites 236/236 (one transient 30ms heartbeat-count flake, green on isolated + batch re-run); tsc clean; build green.
